briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. We will now begin the climate briefing for August 7, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Intensification of Extreme Weather Events and Global Threats
sections.content: Today, reports continued to emerge from various parts of the world indicating the further intensification of extreme weather phenomena due to climate change. Canada experienced massive wildfires, and the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) identified climate change as the cause, refuting former President Trump's claims of inadequate forest management [1, 84, 86, 92, 93]. Consequently, air quality in the U.S. Northwest reached its worst levels, and reports also indicated that the risk of wildfires has doubled due to the climate crisis [15, 90, 98, 99, 101, 102, 105, 114]. Domestically, despite the traditional start of autumn (Ipchu), Seoul's temperature exceeded 40 degrees Celsius for the first time in 8 years, marking a record-breaking heatwave. This combined disaster situation of heatwaves and drought is causing emergencies across Europe in the energy, logistics, and agricultural sectors [19, 26, 75, 110, 111]. Such a climate crisis even raises the possibility of human extinction, urging us to seek fundamental solutions [23].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Efforts for Climate Crisis Adaptation and Social Safety Net Establishment
sections.content: Domestically, various efforts to adapt to the changing climate environment and mitigate damages have been reported. Jeju Province is promoting the distribution of open-field citrus varieties adapted to climate change, while Sangju City is enhancing cultivation stability through apple variety diversification [16, 18]. 'Climate insurance' products designed to compensate for economic losses and illnesses caused by heatwaves are gaining attention, and the necessity of a 'climate safety net' to prepare for heatwaves exceeding 38 degrees Celsius during severe heatwave warnings has been highlighted [21, 27, 29, 38]. Furthermore, Kookmin University is seeking solutions to the climate crisis through international cooperation, including operating field studies in Japan for climate change response and exploring low-carbon and energy transition solutions [3, 17, 24]. The livestock industry is also suffering damages, such as decreased milk production and exacerbated reproductive disorders in dairy cows due to heatwaves, making urgent adaptation measures necessary [25].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Building a Carbon-Neutral Society
sections.content: The movement to expand renewable energy for a transition to a carbon-neutral society is actively underway. Haenam County is developing a carbon-neutral specialized forest in the Mandaesan area, and various local governments, including Osan City and Daejeon Daedeok-gu, are expanding carbon-neutral practice education and eco-friendly activities for citizens and businesses [31, 32, 34, 35, 37, 39, 40, 41, 46, 47, 48]. Particularly in the manufacturing sector, there is a growing trend of renewable energy purchase agreements beyond carbon neutrality declarations, and tax credit support is planned for domestic production in areas such as renewable energy, batteries, semiconductors, and robots [36, 49, 80]. Jeju Province is conceptualizing and launching the construction of a 40 MW 'Green AI Data Center' utilizing surplus renewable energy, making innovative attempts to use renewable energy as the power base for the AI industry [50, 51, 52, 56, 62, 65, 67, 70, 76]. However, while a global solar power transition is taking place, Korea's share of solar power generation remains lower than the global average, indicating the need for additional efforts [69, 73].

sections.title: 🌍 Widespread Impacts of the Climate Crisis and International Discussions
sections.content: The climate crisis is having widespread impacts across natural ecosystems, the economy, and society as a whole. The phenomenon of butterflies worldwide migrating to new habitats due to climate change has been observed [97, 100, 106], and warnings have been issued that 'climateflation' is becoming a reality due to reduced rice harvests, affecting even Korean dinner tables [28, 107]. Furthermore, the possibility that the Dzungar Khanate, the last nomadic empire of Central Asia, collapsed not due to war but due to climate change, has been raised, providing insight into the historical impact of climate on civilizations [12]. Internationally, climate change lawsuits are expected to commence in the U.S. Supreme Court, and legal and academic discussions on climate crisis response are actively progressing, with Rice University and TMC partners securing consortium grants to address climate change and human health issues [85, 108]. China's AI weather solution 'Mazu' is expected to be utilized for climate change response in Africa, and research findings have also been released indicating that climate change increases the likelihood of turbulence during flights [13, 104].

briefing.closing: In today's briefing, we examined the intensification of extreme weather events and various domestic and international efforts to address them. Global cooperation and sustained action are more crucial than ever to overcome the climate crisis. This concludes today's climate briefing.
